$BTC ETFs saw another massive outflow day on Wednesday. But this day ended up closing +1% in the green after a 5% intra day reversal.

Moves like these where the market is flat or up after massive ETF outflow days are generally your first signs to start paying attention.

Of course this day could have been an outlier, but if you see more of these days that usually points to strong absorption and the outflows themselves often reverse from that point too.

Over the years we've seen many local tops and bottoms on strong ETF flows. When price stops moving in the same direction of those flows is when you watch closely.

BITCOIN: WHAT THE MONTHLY RSI IS TELLING US

One of the most interesting patterns in Bitcoin's history is how the monthly RSI has consistently formed lower lows at each major bear market bottom.

2011, 2015, 2018, 2022.

Every cycle has followed the same descending structure, with momentum reaching progressively lower levels during capitulation.

Currently, the monthly RSI is sitting around 42.7, while the historical structure suggests a potential bottom somewhere in the 30–35 region.

Now, looking at this chart, you might think we're relatively close to the bottom.

But here's where people need to be careful.

Being close to a bottom in terms of momentum doesn't necessarily mean we're close in terms of price.

The final stages of a bear market are often the most aggressive. A relatively small decline in the monthly RSI can accompany a substantial decline in Bitcoin's price.

This is typically when the remaining conviction disappears, long-term holders begin questioning their positions, and genuine capitulation takes place.

Of course, historical patterns are not guarantees, and the RSI should never be used in isolation.

However, this structure remains consistent with my broader bearish thesis.

I believe we're approaching the most psychologically challenging phase of this bear market, but we're not there yet.

Don't underestimate the amount of damage the market can do during its final leg down.

The last stretch is often the most brutal.

Patience.

WHY I THINK THIS BEAR MARKET IS DIFFERENT

I think one of the biggest mistakes people are making right now is trying to analyze this bear market through the lens of previous cycles.

The environment has fundamentally changed, and there are several bearish catalysts that deserve far more attention.

1. Bitcoin miners pivoting towards AI.

Some of the largest mining companies are diversifying into AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. Bitcoin mining is no longer their only opportunity to monetize energy and computing infrastructure.

2. Competition for capital.

Artificial intelligence, quantum computing, robotics, and other emerging technologies are competing for the speculative capital and attention that previously flowed into crypto.

Crypto is no longer the only exciting technological investment.

3. Narrative exhaustion.

ICOs, DeFi, NFTs, the metaverse, gaming, memecoins. The industry has burned through countless narratives without delivering enough sustainable value to justify the speculation.

4. Destruction of retail confidence.

Years of scams, insider enrichment, failed projects, and devastating losses have damaged the industry's reputation. Attracting fresh retail capital may become increasingly difficult.

5. Excessive token supply.

There are millions of tokens competing for liquidity. Add continuous token unlocks, emissions, and selling pressure from early investors, and you have a fundamentally challenging environment for altcoins.

6. The macroeconomic environment.

Bitcoin has never experienced a prolonged equity bear market comparable to 2000 or 2008. If the AI bubble bursts and traditional markets enter a sustained downturn, crypto could face an unprecedented macroeconomic stress test.

7. Institutional capital doesn't guarantee permanent demand.

ETFs have made Bitcoin more accessible, but they've also created another channel through which capital can leave during periods of risk aversion. Institutional adoption doesn't eliminate market cycles.

Individually, none of these factors necessarily guarantees a prolonged bear market. Collectively, however, they paint a concerning picture.

Yet people are still using historical cycle models to predict when the bottom will form, how deep the correction will be, and when the next altseason will begin.

Why assume the outcome will be the same when the underlying conditions are so different?

I don't believe crypto is going to disappear. I believe the industry needs a massive structural reset, and only a fraction of today's projects will emerge stronger from it.

In my opinion, this bear market will be remembered not only for the destruction of capital, but also for the destruction of confidence.

And confidence takes considerably longer to recover than price.

That's why I expect this bear market to be particularly painful, not just in terms of price, but also in terms of duration.

The real capitulation is still ahead of us.

In 2021 I called 18k the bottom, bought a lot of size there and I was sure we would not break below. Some weeks later Bitcoin went to 16k, so what did I do, capitulate? Sell? Time will tell.

$BTC Looking at all the previous bear market bottoms, after the first impulse you usually get a retrace of at least the .618 and often deeper. That is where we are now.

The 2018 and 2022 bottoms did take about 2 months to play out after the last leg down.

The 2020 covid crash resolved much faster but that also was a very unique situation.

Never have we seen a direct V shape without some kind of retest lower after the initial bounce. Even though zooming out might look like that, intraday/week we have had a retest every time. So this is normal.

For the sake of this example, assuming the 21st of November was the bottom (no one knows neither do I) we could also argue that this "bottoming" was already in process since June when price already hit this level. Even though we can see that has never been the case anyways. I agree, things look very weak relatively, but also that is normal for these situations.

In the end no one knows, maybe we get another leg down, maybe we do not. All I'm showing here is how previous major bottoms looked and that you always see a retrace that goes pretty deep.

Just for informational purposes, personally not sure what the next week(s) will bring us. Still believe anything around this region is solid high timeframe value for $BTC if you believe in it long term. Long road ahead of us though that's for sure.

A says B lies. B says C lies. C says A and B both lie. Who tells the truth?

Stop here and think about it. What's your answer?

.

.

.

At first I thought it was impossible, that there had to be several valid answers. I felt stupid for a moment and said "probably C, but it could be any of them."

Then I asked my quant, a PhD in quantum physics with a 160+ IQ and several Millennium Prizes to his name. He said: "Try inverting the question, young one."

Ohhh. Forget who tells the truth. Who is lying? In what scenario do we get one truth and two lies?

If C is honest, then A and B both lie. But if A lies, B is telling the truth. Contradiction. C is a liar.

If A is honest, then B lies, which makes C honest. But C says A lies. Contradiction again. A is a liar.

That leaves B. If B is honest, C lies and A lies too. Everything fits. 

Trading works the same way. Instead of asking "why should I take this trade?", ask "why shouldn't I? What could go wrong? Should I cut it?"

I wrote about this years ago, then stopped practicing it. It's old wisdom, and it's as relevant as ever. 

It works at home too. If your wife asks "Should we go on a trip? Should we go shopping?", reply: "Should we stay home? Should we avoid materialism?" 

Invert the question. Often. Automatically.

$BTC The New York Market open is coming up.

These have been brutal for BTC with it setting the high in the first 15 minutes most of the times and seeing an average decline of -1.07% during the 6.5 hours the market is open.

The past 5 trading sessions have been especially tough as you can see on the chart.

With Spot ETFs selling ~$500M a day it is easy to see where at least part of that selling pressure is coming from.

So prepare for the worst but be very much on the look out for when this changes. Any signs of relative strength (for more than just a few hours), ETF spot flows reversing and/or price not going down on bad news will be the first signs to watch out for.

Until that happens you can play it safe and remain patient with your trades.

Another big headline.

Funnily enough, the TradFi pre-market and crypto price action the day before these massive headlines have been pretty indicative of whatever news has been dropping.

Could be a coincidence of course, but it has been happening a few times too many for that at this point.

Oil has been moving like that too for months. Can be up or down a lot, then a headline drops confirming whatever price action was preceding it, usually that in itself is then the reversal point and some hours or days later you get some headline completely supporting the other side.

tl;dr
Following these things have generally made you buy a lot of local tops and sell a lot of local bottoms. Because the move happened before the headline a lot of the times.

The controversy surrounding Ansem brings us back to the same recurring problem in crypto: influencers using their influence to enrich themselves at the expense of their own audience.

But the problem goes much deeper than any individual.

In my opinion, crypto broke the moment anyone could create a token in minutes, manufacture a narrative around it, and monetize speculation without delivering anything of real value.

We created an ecosystem where influence became more profitable than innovation, and where extracting liquidity became more rewarding than building something meaningful.

And unfortunately, it's usually the least experienced investors and those with the least money who end up paying the price.

I also want to take this opportunity to make something clear: you will never see me putting myself in that position.

As I explained in a previous post, which I encourage you to read, from 2027 onwards, I won't even be covering altcoins or individual projects anymore.

It's a personal decision based on respect for my audience and the responsibility that comes with having a platform.

Having influence is a privilege. Exploiting it for personal financial gain at the expense of those who trust you is a choice.

Crypto has enormous potential, but until the industry stops rewarding this kind of behavior, it will continue to destroy its own credibility.

I genuinely hope things change in the future.

This industry could be so much better than what it has become.

BREAKTHROUGH IN BITCOIN CRYPTOGRAPHY: RESEARCHERS UNVEIL FIRST PRACTICAL WITNESS ENCRYPTION FOR GENERAL NP

Researchers at Byzantine Research and Stanford University have introduced Praxis, a new cryptographic scheme that could unlock major advances in Bitcoin scaling, trust-minimized bridges, and smart contracts.

Witness encryption allows information to be encrypted so that only someone possessing a valid mathematical proof can decrypt it.

At 100-bit security, Praxis achieves:

Ciphertext size: Under 8 GB
Encryption and decryption: Seconds
Security: Formally verified in Lean 4 under specified cryptographic assumptions

Compared with previous constructions, Praxis reduces ciphertext size and encryption costs by more than 10 orders of magnitude, and decryption costs by more than 6 orders of magnitude.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR BITCOIN:

The researchers’ primary motivation is enabling non-interactive proof verification on Bitcoin without requiring challengers or operators.

This could potentially enable:

More trust-minimized Bitcoin bridges: Reducing reliance on third-party operators and honest challengers to prevent fraudulent transactions.

Improved Bitcoin scaling: Enabling more sophisticated off-chain computation with fewer interactive verification requirements.

More powerful Bitcoin smart contracts: Opening the door to new applications and conditional execution mechanisms without necessarily requiring changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules.

Reduced trust assumptions: Allowing certain cryptographic proofs to be used without depending on an independent party to monitor and challenge invalid claims.

The breakthrough could address one of the major limitations of existing Bitcoin scaling proposals, including BitVM-style systems that rely on interactive fraud proofs and honest challengers.

While Praxis remains an early-stage research result rather than a production-ready Bitcoin solution, it represents a significant advance toward making witness encryption practical.

Paper: https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2971

$BTC TAKES THE DOWNSIDE, MISSES THE UPSIDE.

Bear years always look the same. Small gains when stocks rally, full losses when they drop.

But look at the pre-halving years. In 2019 and 2023, Bitcoin went UP even on the weeks the S&P went down.

If the cycle rhymes, 2027 is when Bitcoin stops bleeding with stocks.

Until then, the rallies are for selling, not chasing.

BITCOIN: THE MOST IMPORTANT SUPPORT LEVEL ON THE CHART

There's a reason Bitcoin keeps bouncing from this area.

And it's not a coincidence.

We're currently sitting on what I consider to be the most important horizontal support level in Bitcoin's entire market structure.

$58,500.

Look at the monthly chart.

This level has played a crucial role in Bitcoin's price action for years, and losing it on a monthly closing basis would be an extremely significant technical development.

In my view, a confirmed monthly close below this support would immediately put $30K into focus as the next major downside target.

Of course, we're talking about monthly candles. The market isn't going to give everyone 30 days to react once the breakdown starts.

And that's precisely why we're seeing such aggressive reactions every time BTC approaches this area.

Buyers understand its importance.

But here's the bad news for the bulls.

We've already tested this support three times.

And every time a support level gets tested, there's a risk that the remaining buying pressure becomes weaker.

The more times buyers are forced to defend the same level, the more vulnerable that level can become.

Eventually, one side runs out of ammunition.

$58,500 is the level you should be watching very closely into this monthly close.

Because when we lose it, the entire conversation around Bitcoin's downside potential will change dramatically.

Mark this level on your charts.

It could define the next major phase of this bear market.

Hope you understand.
